quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When you slow down or stop, should you use both brakes?

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the most stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What can help if your drive chain slips?
questions.explanation: If your chain slips, tightening it may help. If tightening does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: Which is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding a motorcycle. Good protective gear includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle fit a rider?

options.text: The rider can touch the ground with their feet while seated.
The seat is level with the rider's waist.
The seat is 10 inches above the rider's waist.
The seat is 10 inches below the rider's waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider can touch the ground with their feet while seated.
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle allows you to reach the ground with your feet while sitting on the seat. Keep your feet on the footrests while riding.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rear brake on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Use your mirrors to see all of your surroundings.
Point in the direction you are changing.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding, what happens?

options.text: The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: Downshifting to a lower gear is similar to:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have a manual transmission. When you downshift to a lower gear, you slow down.

questions.question: Is it legal to ride between two vehicles moving in the same direction?

options.text: Yes, during the day to prevent traffic jams.
Yes, if the motorcyclist is comfortable with it.

questions.explanation: In Oregon, it is illegal for motorcycles to pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Sit with your arms holding you up instead of steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you must stretch to reach the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Press your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced in turns. Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Sit close enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handlebars. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good way for a rider to increase their visibility?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials. Use your headlight at all times. Use your turn signals and brake light properly. Waving does not increase your visibility.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located near the right handlebar. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: A group of riders should merge onto a highway in:
questions.explanation: Use staggered formation for normal riding. Switch to single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Drivers on an entrance ramp may not see you on the highway. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane. You are not responsible for being seen.
Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
Weave within your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space to enter traffic safely. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if you can do so safely. If no other lane is available, slow down to create space for the merging driver.

questions.question: Usually, a good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may make them follow you faster and increase danger.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's total braking power does the front brake supply?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only on slippery surfaces.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use if used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.question: Studies show that when motorcycles have their headlights on during the day:

options.text: They are not as easy to see as other vehicles.
They are more visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
They are less safe than with headlights off.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride to help other drivers see you. Motorcycles with headlights on during the day are twice as likely to be noticed.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the edge of the road, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to the motorcycle. This extra weight requires more braking force. Stopping takes longer when going downhill than on flat ground.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a quick stop, apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How should you sit to control a motorcycle properly?

options.text: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up.
Sit far back on the seat so your arms stay straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to support your body. Your arms should bend slightly at the handle grips. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, what should you assume about other drivers?

options.text: Assume they see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Focus only on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make them notice you.

questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still fail to notice them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: What reduces head and neck injuries the most?
questions.explanation: A high-quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is the best protection a rider has in an accident.
